inline.s: World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may all beings born in my land have lives not cut short, but live for a hundred thousand koṭis of nayutas of kalpas, and all shall be made to attain utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may all beings born in my land hear no name of evil; but hearing of the immeasurable and countless Buddha-lands, where there is no name and no designation, no mark and no form, and nothing to be praised, may they harbor no doubt or slander, their bodies and minds unmoved, and all shall be made to attain utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, all beings who seek birth in my land, who recollect my name and title, who bring forth a mind of utmost sincerity, firm and without retreat — at the end of their lives I shall cause countless monks to appear before them and surround them, and come to welcome them. In a moment they shall be born in my land, and all shall be made to attain utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may all beings of the ten directions, in immeasurable, boundless, countless worlds, who hear my name and title and bring forth the bodhi mind, who plant all roots of goodness and seek rebirth as they wish in the Buddha-lands, be born in every one of them, and all shall be made to attain utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may all beings born in my land all possess the thirty-two marks of a great man, and in one life be made to attain utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, all beings born in my land who have great vows and do not yet wish to become Buddhas but would be bodhisattvas — by my majestic power I shall cause them to teach and transform all beings. May they all bring forth a mind of faith and cultivate the bodhi practices: the practice of Samantabhadra, the practice of still quiescence, the pure brahma practice, the supreme practice, and every good practice; and all shall be made to attain utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may all beings born in my land serve and make offering everywhere to immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Buddhas, planting all roots of goodness. Whatever they seek as they wish shall be fulfilled without exception, and all shall be made to attain utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may all the bodhisattvas in my land all accomplish all wisdom and skillfully expound the hidden essentials of all dharmas, and before long swiftly accomplish utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may all the bodhisattvas dwelling in my jeweled land bring forth a courageous and valiant mind and wield great spiritual penetration, going to the immeasurable, boundless, countless worlds and among all the Buddha-lands, and with pearls and jewelled garlands, jeweled canopies, banners and streamers, clothing and bedding, food and drink and medicines, fragrant flowers and music, make offering and service; and turning this toward bodhi, may they swiftly accomplish utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may all the bodhisattvas dwelling in my jeweled land bring forth the great mind of the path, wishing with pearls and jewelled garlands, jeweled canopies, banners and streamers, clothing and bedding, food and drink and medicines, fragrant flowers and music, to serve and make offering to the immeasurable and boundless World-Honored Buddhas of other worlds, and yet be unable to go there. I at that time, by the power of my past vows, shall cause those World-Honored Buddhas of other worlds each to extend their arms into my land and receive these offerings, causing those bodhisattvas swiftly to accomplish utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may all the bodhisattvas dwelling in my jeweled land, following the joy of their own hearts, without leaving this realm, wish with pearls and jewelled garlands, jeweled canopies, banners and streamers, clothing and bedding, food and drink and medicines, fragrant flowers and music, to make offering to the immeasurable Buddhas of other directions. And again they think: if the Buddhas must stretch out their arms and come here to receive the offerings, the Buddhas are put to toil, and this brings me no benefit. When they form this thought, I by my spiritual power shall cause these offerings to arrive of themselves before those Buddhas in other directions, one by one as offerings. Then those bodhisattvas shall before long all accomplish utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may all the bodhisattvas dwelling in my jeweled land be sixteen yojanas in bodily height and obtain the strength of Nārāyaṇa. Their bodily marks shall be fair and dignified, their radiance shining, their roots of goodness complete, and they shall accomplish utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may all the bodhisattvas dwelling in my jeweled land, for the sake of all beings, master the Dharma treasury, establish boundless, all-embracing wisdom, cut off every fetter, and all realize and accomplish utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may all the bodhisattvas dwelling in my jeweled land, with hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of various precious treasures, fashion incense burners, from the lowest reaches of the earth up to the sphere of space, and ever with priceless sandalwood incense pervade and make offering to the Buddhas of the ten directions, causing them swiftly to accomplish utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may the Buddha-land in which I dwell be vast, broad, majestic, and pure, luminous and clear as a mirror, able to reflect immeasurable, boundless, all Buddha-lands. Beings who behold it shall bring forth a rare and precious mind, and before long swiftly accomplish utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may all the bodhisattvas dwelling in my jeweled land, through the six periods of day and night, ever receive happiness surpassing that of the devas, enter the gate of the samādhi of equality, and with bodily radiance illumine boundless worlds, and before long attain utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, if among all the women of the ten directions, in immeasurable, boundless, countless worlds, there are those who weary of and turn from the female body, who hear my name and title, bring forth a pure mind, take refuge, and bow in homage — at the end of their lives they shall at once be born in my land, attain a man’s body, and all shall be made to attain utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may the hearers and solitary realizers of the ten directions, in immeasurable, boundless, countless Buddha-lands, who hear my name and title, cultivate and uphold the pure precepts, firm and without retreat, swiftly sit in the place of enlightenment and accomplish utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may all the bodhisattvas of the ten directions, in immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, unequaled Buddha-lands, who hear my name and title, bow with all five parts of the body to the ground and worship in homage, and further obtain from all beings in heaven and among humans respect and reverence, closeness and service, thereby increasing their merit and accomplishing utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may all beings who bring forth a pure and faithful mind, and who for monks and brahmins dye robes, wash robes, cut robes, sew robes, and make monastic garments, whether with their own hands or causing others to do so, and who, having done so, dedicate the merit — may what such a person feels be this: for eighty-one births to obtain the finest garments, with all things in abundance about them; and in their final body to be born in my land and accomplish utmost, perfect bodhi.

Thereupon the monk Dharmākara said to the World-Honored One: When I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may all beings who hear my name and title forever leave behind the fever of affliction and gain coolness of mind, practice right faith and right conduct, and be born in my land; seated beneath a jeweled tree they shall realize the patient acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas and accomplish utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may all the hosts of bodhisattvas in all Buddha-lands of the ten directions, upon hearing my name and title, at that very time realize the samādhi of stillness. Abiding in that concentration, in a single thought they shall see immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable World-Honored Buddhas, serve and make offering to them, and accomplish utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may the hearers and bodhisattvas of all Buddha-lands in the ten directions, upon hearing my name and title, realize the patient acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas, accomplish all equal roots of goodness, and abide without effort, far from any further cultivation; and before long they shall be made to attain utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may all the hosts of bodhisattvas in all Buddha-lands of the ten directions, having heard my name, bring forth a rare and precious mind. Such a person shall at once obtain the bodhisattva samādhi of universality. Abiding in this concentration, in a single thought they shall reach immeasurable, countless, inconceivable Buddha-lands, revere, honor, and make offering to those Buddhas, and accomplish utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may all the bodhisattvas in my land, whether they delight in expounding the Dharma or delight in hearing the Dharma, whether they manifest the bases of spiritual power or go to other directions, cultivate as they wish, and nothing shall fail of completion; and all shall be made to realize utmost, perfect bodhi.

World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and accomplished true enlightenment, may all in the ten directions and in every Buddha-land who hear my name at that very time obtain the first patience, the second patience, and even the patient acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas, and accomplish utmost, perfect bodhi.
Thereupon the monk Dharmākara, having brought forth these vows before that Buddha, by the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha straightway spoke in verse:
Before the Buddha I now bring forth my vow of truth.
To gain the Buddha’s body of the ten powers, in majesty and virtue without equal.
Again to be a great king, wealthy and at ease.
With every kind of wealth and treasure, to give freely to the poor and suffering.
To cause all those multitudes of beings, through the long night, to be free of sorrow and affliction.
To bring forth every root of goodness, and accomplish the fruit of bodhi.
When I attain true enlightenment, my name shall be Immeasurable Life.
Beings who hear this name shall all come into my land.
Like the Buddha’s golden body, all my wondrous marks complete.
And with a heart of great compassion, to benefit every kind of being.
May the light of my wisdom broadly illumine the lands of the ten directions.
To destroy in all beings the darkness of greed, anger, and affliction.
May hells, ghosts, and animals all forsake the suffering of the three evil paths.
And be born in my land, cultivating the practices of purity.
To gain that body of radiance, shining everywhere like the Buddha.
The light of sun, moon, and precious jewels — their brightness cannot compare.
May I in future ages ever be a teacher of devas and humans.
In a hundred koṭis of worlds, to give the lion’s roar.
Like those Buddhas of the past, in the compassionate course they walked.
Vast, immeasurable, and boundless, koṭis upon koṭis of beings.
Fulfilling the vows made long ago, all shall become Buddhas.
When these great vows were spoken, the three thousand great thousand worlds
Quaked and trembled throughout the ten directions; in the heavens among devas and humans
A rain of every flower was scattered, sandalwood and eaglewood.
They praised that great monk: his vow-power is most rare.
He is certain to become a Buddha, broadly benefiting the realms of beings.

Again, Ānanda, when the monk Dharmākara had brought forth these vows before the Tathāgata Lokeśvararāja, together with devas and humans, Māra and Brahmā, monks and brahmins, asuras, and the rest, he dwelt in true wisdom, brave and vigorous in effort, cultivating immeasurable merit. Adorning the Buddha-land, he entered samādhi. Through a great asaṃkhyeya kalpa he cultivated the bodhisattva practices. He gave rise to no mind of stinginess or greed, no mind of anger or hatred, no mind of ignorance; nor had he any thought of desire, thought of anger, thought of delusion, or thought of form, sound, smell, taste, or touch. His mind was never confused, his speech never mute or halting, his body never indolent; he delighted only in recollecting the roots of goodness cultivated by the Buddhas of the past, and in walking the course of stillness. Far from falsehood, he firmly upheld the discipline. Ever with loving words he benefited beings. Toward Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha he was faithful, reverent, and respectful, gentle and compliant. By the gate of ultimate truth he planted the roots of every virtue. He comprehended emptiness, marklessness, wishlessness, non-action, non-arising, and non-ceasing. He well guarded the karma of speech and did not mock the faults of others. He well guarded the karma of body and did not transgress the discipline. He well guarded the karma of mind, pure and undefiled. Toward all cities and towns, villages and settlements, men and women, servants and retainers, gold and silver and precious treasures, and even form, sound, smell, taste, and touch, he was wholly unattached. Ever with giving, precepts, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom — the practice of the six pāramitās — he brought benefit and joy to beings. His conduct was complete in every model, his roots of goodness perfected. In whatever place he was born, treasure vaults of immeasurable, countless hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of precious gems welled up from the earth. He gathered and received immeasurable, countless hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings and caused them to bring forth the mind of utmost, perfect bodhi. Such was his practice: immeasurable and boundless, beyond all telling.

Again, Ānanda, while the monk Dharmākara walked the bodhisattva practices, he was reverent and respectful in the presence of all Buddhas, serving and making offering without ever a break. As the Four Great Kings he ever went to the Buddha’s presence with reverence and homage, serving and making offering. As Śakra, lord of the devas, he ever went to the Buddha’s presence with reverence and homage, serving and making offering. As the Yāma Heaven King, the King of the Tuṣita Heaven, the King of the Heaven of Enjoying Conjurations, the King of the Heaven of Enjoying the Conjurations of Others, and even the Great Brahmā Kings and the rest, he ever went to the Buddha’s presence with reverence and homage, serving and making offering.

Again, Ānanda, dwelling in Jambudvīpa, he was a wheel-turning king who received the consecration of anointment, and also a great minister, a noble of official clans, and the like. He ever went to the Buddha’s presence with reverence and homage, serving and making offering. As a kṣatriya or a brahmin and the rest, he ever went to the Buddha’s presence with reverence and homage, serving and making offering. Thus for immeasurable, countless hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of kalpas he drew near to the Buddhas and planted the roots of every virtue, gathering the utmost, perfect bodhi.

Again, Ānanda, while the monk Dharmākara walked the bodhisattva practices, from his mouth there ever came the fragrance of sandalwood, and from every pore of his body the fragrance of the utpala lotus. That fragrance pervaded immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable nayutas of hundreds of thousands of yojanas. Beings who smelled that fragrance all brought forth the mind of utmost, perfect bodhi.

Again, Ānanda, while the monk Dharmākara walked the bodhisattva practices, he was fair and dignified in countenance, fully endowed with the thirty-two marks and the eighty excellent characteristics. Moreover, both his arms were adorned with every precious treasure, and from his hands there ever came every kind of clothing, every kind of food and drink, every kind of banner and streamer, every kind of parasol and canopy, all kinds of music, and even every kind of thing that is most needful. He brought benefit and joy to all beings and caused them to bring forth the mind of utmost, perfect bodhi.

Thereupon Ānanda, having heard the Buddha speak of the practices of that monk Dharmākara, said to the World-Honored One: “Was the monk Dharmākara a Buddha of the past, a Buddha of the future, or a Buddha of the present?”

The World-Honored One told him: “That Buddha Tathāgata comes from nowhere and goes nowhere; he neither arises nor ceases, and is not past, present, or future. But to repay his vows and deliver beings, he now abides in the western direction. A hundred thousand koṭis of nayutas of Buddha-lands away from Jambudvīpa, there is a world named Ultimate Bliss. The Buddha is named Immeasurable Life. Ten kalpas have passed since he accomplished Buddhahood. He has immeasurable, countless bodhisattvas, great beings, and immeasurable, countless hosts of hearers, who revere and surround him as he speaks the Dharma for them. The radiance of that Buddha illumines eastward Buddha-lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, a hundred thousand koṭis of nayutas of them, beyond all measure. So too in the south, the west, and the north, and in the four intermediate directions, above and below, it is likewise.”

Again, Ānanda, the circle of transformed light of that Buddha Immeasurable Life extends one yojana, two yojanas, three yojanas, or a hundred yojanas, a thousand yojanas, a hundred thousand yojanas, or koṭis of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of yojanas, even to pervading immeasurable, boundless, countless Buddha-lands.

Again, Ānanda, this light is now named the Light of Immeasurable Life, the Unobstructed Light, the Ever-Shining Light, the Unfailing Light, the Light of Benefit, the Light of Loving Joy, the Light of Peace and Stillness, the Light of Liberation, the Unequaled Light, the Inconceivable Light, the Light Surpassing Sun and Moon, the Light That Outshines All Lights of the World, and the Stainless Pure Light.

Thus does this light shine universally over all worlds of the ten directions. Devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans and non-humans, and the rest, seeing this light, bring forth the bodhi mind and gain benefit and joy thereby. The Buddha told Ānanda: Though I were to abide a kalpa speaking of the merit and benefit of this light, I could not finish.

Again, Ānanda, the Tathāgata Immeasurable Life has such a host of hearers — a hundred thousand myriads, a hundred thousand, a million; one koṭi, a hundred koṭis, a thousand koṭis; a count of kiṃkaras, a count of bimbas, a count of nayutas, a count of ayutas, a count of vivāhas, a count of vaṣaṇas, a count of raṅgas, a count of asaṃkhyeyas, ten asaṃkhyeyas, a hundred asaṃkhyeyas, a thousand asaṃkhyeyas, a hundred thousand asaṃkhyeyas, a count of amanyas, a count of inconceivables — such are his immeasurable, countless hosts of hearers; by metaphor or by reckoning they cannot be counted. Ānanda, that great Maudgalyāyana, foremost in spiritual penetration, could know in a single day and night the number of every boy and girl in the three thousand great thousand worlds. Suppose a hundred thousand koṭis of hearers all possessed the power of spiritual penetration like great Maudgalyāyana, and each of those hearers lived a hundred thousand koṭis of nayutas of years, and with all that lifespan did the counting — even so, of those hearers they could not count a hundredth part, not a single part.

Again, Ānanda, suppose the great ocean were eighty-four thousand yojanas deep and immeasurably wide. Suppose a person plucked out one hair, split it into a hundred koṭis of parts as fine as motes of dust, and with each mote dipped out water from the sea. The water clinging to the mote would be of that measure; and when every hair-mote had thus been dipped out, what do you think? Would the water on the hair-motes be more, or the water in the sea?”
Ānanda said to the Buddha: “World-Honored One, the water drawn out on a hair-mote does not come to half a handful; the water of the sea is immeasurable.”

The Buddha said to Ānanda: “The host of hearers such as Maudgalyāyana and the rest, though they spent their whole lives counting, could know only as much as the water on a hair-mote. What they could not finish counting is as the water of the sea. Thus that Buddha has such immeasurable, incalculable śrāvaka disciples. Moreover, that Buddha-land is greatly wealthy and immeasurable. It knows only happiness; there is no suffering of any kind. There are no hells, no hungry ghosts, no animals, no realm of Yama, and no retribution of the eight difficulties. There are only pure bodhisattvas, great beings, and hosts of hearers.

Again, Ānanda, that Buddha-land has all kinds of jeweled pillars, each adorned with hundreds of thousands of precious treasures. There are golden pillars, silver pillars, crystal pillars, beryl pillars, pearl pillars, mother-of-pearl pillars, and carnelian pillars. There are also pillars of the two treasures, gold and silver; pillars of the three treasures, gold, silver, and crystal; pillars of the four treasures, gold, silver, crystal, and beryl; pillars of the five treasures, gold, silver, crystal, beryl, and pearls; pillars of the six treasures, gold, silver, crystal, beryl, pearls, and mother-of-pearl; and pillars of the seven treasures, gold, silver, crystal, beryl, pearls, mother-of-pearl, and carnelian.

Again, Ānanda, that Buddha-land also has all kinds of jeweled trees. Their roots, stems, branches, and trunks are made of gold; their flowers, leaves, and fruits are transformed from silver. There are also jeweled trees whose roots, stems, branches, and trunks are made of silver, and whose flowers, leaves, and fruits are transformed from crystal. There are also jeweled trees whose roots, stems, branches, and trunks are made of crystal, and whose flowers, leaves, and fruits are transformed from beryl. There are also jeweled trees whose roots, stems, branches, and leaves are made of beryl, and whose flowers, leaves, and fruits are transformed from pearls. There are also jeweled trees whose roots, stems, branches, and trunks are made of pearls, and whose flowers, leaves, and fruits are transformed from mother-of-pearl. There are also jeweled trees whose roots, stems, branches, and trunks are made of mother-of-pearl, and whose flowers, leaves, and fruits are transformed from carnelian. There are also jeweled trees whose roots, stems, branches, and trunks are made of carnelian, and whose flowers, leaves, and fruits are transformed from gold. There are also jeweled trees with gold as root, silver as trunk, crystal as branches, beryl as crown, pearls as leaves, mother-of-pearl as flowers, and carnelian as fruit. There are also jeweled trees with silver as root, crystal as trunk, beryl as branches, pearls as crown, mother-of-pearl as leaves, carnelian as flowers, and gold as fruit. There are also jeweled trees with crystal as root, beryl as trunk, pearls as branches, mother-of-pearl as crown, carnelian as leaves, gold as flowers, and silver as fruit. There are also jeweled trees with beryl as root, pearls as trunk, mother-of-pearl as branches, carnelian as crown, gold as leaves, silver as flowers, and crystal as fruit. There are also jeweled trees with pearls as root, mother-of-pearl as trunk, carnelian as branches, gold as crown, silver as leaves, crystal as flowers, and beryl as fruit. There are also jeweled trees with mother-of-pearl as root, carnelian as trunk, gold as branches, silver as crown, crystal as leaves, beryl as flowers, and pearls as fruit. There are also jeweled trees with carnelian as root, gold as trunk, silver as branches, crystal as crown, beryl as leaves, pearls as flowers, and mother-of-pearl as fruit. Thus the Land of Ultimate Bliss has its rows of trees of the seven treasures.

Again, Ānanda, that Buddha-land is pure and majestically adorned, broad, level, and even. There are no hills or ridges, no pits or pits and thorns, no gravel, sand, earth, or stone, no such mountains as the Black Mountain, the Snow Mountain, the Jewel Mountain, the Golden Mountain, Mount Sumeru, the Iron Ring Mountain, or the Great Iron Ring Mountain; only gold is its ground.

Thereupon Ānanda, having heard these words, said to the World-Honored One: “The Heaven of the Four Great Kings and the Heaven of the Thirty-Three dwell relying on Mount Sumeru, king of mountains. On what then do the Yāma Heaven and the rest rely to dwell?”
The Buddha told Ānanda: “Do the Yāma Heaven and the Tuṣita Heaven, and even all the heavens of the form realm and formless realm, dwell relying on the sphere of space?”
Ānanda said: “The sphere of space is unobstructed; how can they rely on it to dwell? Action, cause, and karmic retribution are inconceivable.”

The Buddha told Ānanda: “The karmic retribution of your own body is also inconceivable. The karmic retribution of beings is also inconceivable. The sagely power of the Buddhas is inconceivable. Though that Buddha-land has no great ocean, it has springs and rivers flowing and joining everywhere. Their waters are sometimes ten yojanas wide, twenty yojanas, thirty yojanas, even a hundred thousand yojanas, and twelve yojanas deep. Their waters are pure, endowed with the eight virtues, and give forth subtle and wondrous sounds, like the sound of a hundred thousand myriads of kinds of music, pervading all Buddha-lands. All beings who hear them are comforted and delighted and gain great happiness. Moreover, on both banks of those waters there are countless sandalwood trees and auspicious-fruit trees, whose flowers are ever fragrant and whose radiance shines. When beings cross these waters, some wish the water to reach their feet, some wish it to reach their knees, even some wish it to reach their necks; some wish it cold, some warm; some wish the current swift, some slow — each of these waters follows the minds of beings and causes them to receive happiness. Moreover, from within the water come all kinds of sounds: the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, the sound of the Sangha, the sound that stills, the sound of no nature, the sound of the pāramitās, the sound of power, the sound of fearlessness, the sound of penetration, the sound of no practice, the sound of non-arising, the sound of non-ceasing, the sound of stillness, the sound of great compassion, the sound of great pity, the sound of joy and equanimity, and the sound of consecration. Such subtle and wondrous sounds as these it gives forth. Having heard them, beings bring forth a pure mind and are free of all discrimination. Upright and equal, they mature their roots of goodness and never retreat from the mind of utmost, perfect bodhi.

Moreover, in that Buddha-land, those born there never hear the sound of hells, the sound of hungry ghosts, the sound of animals, the sound of yakṣas, the sound of quarreling, the sound of harsh speech, the sound of tale-bearing, the sound of taking life, the sound of theft, or any evil sound. And those beings are fair and dignified in countenance, with immeasurable merit. Their wisdom is clear and penetrating, their spiritual penetration at ease. Palaces and pavilions, gardens and groves, pools and ponds, clothing and bedding — all are like those of the Heaven of Enjoying the Conjurations of Others; every supreme instrument of happiness is fully provided.

Again, Ānanda, when the beings of that land think of fragrant flowers and the like, wishing to make offering to the Buddhas, at the very moment they form the thought, fragrant flowers and jewelled garlands, perfumed ointments and powdered incense, banners and streamers and parasols, and all kinds of music, arrive as they wish, filling the Buddha-land; and if they think of food and drink and medicines, clothing and bedding, crowns for the head and earrings, pearl nets and the rest, these too arrive with the thought and pervade the Buddha-land. And again, when they think of maṇi jewels and the like to adorn palaces and pavilions, halls and chambers and houses, whether great or small, high or low, at the moment they so think they appear before them as they wish, with nothing lacking.

Again, Ānanda, suppose a person of little wealth and few treasures were to stand before a kṣatriya king who has received the consecration of anointment: all his majesty and power would not appear. Again, when a kṣatriya stands before Śakra, lord of the devas, all his majesty and power would not appear. Again, when Śakra stands before the Heaven of Enjoying the Conjurations of Others, all his majesty and power would not appear. Again, when the Heaven of Enjoying the Conjurations of Others and the heavens of the form and formless realms, with all their majesty, stand before the Tathāgata Immeasurable Life and his Land of Ultimate Bliss, none of it appears. Thus the merit and adornment of that land is inconceivable.

Again, Ānanda, in that Buddha-land, at every mealtime a fragrant breeze arises of itself and stirs the jeweled trees. As the trees brush and touch one another, they give forth subtle and wondrous sounds, proclaiming suffering, emptiness, impermanence, and no-self, and the pāramitās. And again the breeze blows down the flowers of the trees, which fall upon the ground and cover the whole Buddha-land to a height of seven man-lengths. Level and fair, soft and luminous and smooth, when people walk back and forth and their feet press that ground, it sinks four finger-breadths, and like kācilinda cloth it is soothing to the touch. When the mealtime has passed, those jeweled flowers hide themselves in the ground and do not appear. In a moment a wind rises again, blows down the flowers of the trees, and spreads them over the ground as before, with no difference. In the first watch of the night and the last watch of the night it is likewise.

Again, Ānanda, that Buddha-land has no darkness. It has no stars, no sun and moon, no day and night, no taking and no relinquishing, no discrimination; it is wholly one, without mixture, knowing only purity and supreme happiness. If there are good men or good women who have been born there, or shall be born there, such a person is certain to realize utmost, perfect bodhi. What do you think? In that Buddha-land there are no three kinds of loss: first, the mind is without falsehood; second, the stage is without retrogression; third, goodness is without waste.

Again, Ānanda, in the east there are worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, whose Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, put forth the mark of the broad and long tongue, send forth immeasurable light, and speak words of truth, praising the inconceivable merit of the Buddha Immeasurable Life. In the south too there are worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, whose Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, put forth the mark of the broad and long tongue, send forth immeasurable light, and speak words of truth, praising the inconceivable merit of the Buddha Immeasurable Life. In the west too there are worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, whose Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, put forth the mark of the broad and long tongue, send forth immeasurable light, and speak words of truth, praising the inconceivable merit of the Buddha Immeasurable Life. In the north too there are worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, whose Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, put forth the mark of the broad and long tongue, send forth immeasurable light, and speak words of truth, praising the inconceivable merit of the Buddha Immeasurable Life. So too in the four intermediate directions, above and below, in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, put forth the mark of the broad and long tongue, send forth immeasurable light, and speak words of truth, praising the inconceivable merit of the Buddha Immeasurable Life. Ānanda, what do you think? They wish to cause beings to hear that Buddha’s name, bring forth a pure mind, recollect and uphold it, take refuge and make offering, and seek birth in that land. At the end of their lives such people all attain rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss and do not retrogress from utmost, perfect bodhi.

Again, Ānanda, if there are good men or good women who hear this sutra, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, copy and make offering to it, continuing day and night without cease, and seek birth in that land — at the end of such a person’s life the Tathāgata Immeasurable Life, together with the hosts of sages, shall appear before them, and in a moment they shall attain rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss and shall not retrogress from utmost, perfect bodhi.

Again, Ānanda, if there are good men or good women who have brought forth the bodhi mind, who uphold all the precepts and firmly keep them without transgression, who benefit beings and dedicate to them all the roots of goodness they have cultivated, causing them to gain peace and happiness, and who recollect the Tathāgata Immeasurable Life of the west and that Buddha-land — at the end of such a person’s life, with a countenance like the Buddha’s and every kind of adornment, they shall be born in the jeweled land, surrounded by sages and holy ones, swiftly hearing the Dharma, and shall never retrogress from utmost, perfect bodhi.

Again, Ānanda, if there are good men or good women who bring forth ten kinds of mind — namely, first, not to steal; second, not to take life; third, not to commit sexual misconduct; fourth, not to speak falsely; fifth, not to speak frivolously; sixth, not to speak harshly; seventh, not to speak with a forked tongue; eighth, not to be greedy; ninth, not to be angry; tenth, not to be deluded — and who thus, day and night, contemplate the Land of Ultimate Bliss and the Buddha Immeasurable Life, his various merits and various adornments, and with single-minded resolve take refuge, bow in homage, and make offering — at the end of such a person’s life, unalarmed and unafraid, with a mind not inverted, they shall at once attain rebirth in that Buddha-land. There are immeasurable, countless World-Honored Buddhas who praise the merit and name of the Buddha Immeasurable Life. Having heard this Dharma, such a one shall never retrogress from utmost, perfect bodhi.

Again, Ānanda, in the eastern Buddha-lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, in each and every land, there are immeasurable, countless bodhisattvas, great beings, and immeasurable, countless hosts of hearers, who with fragrant flowers, banners and streamers, and jeweled canopies come to make offering to the Buddha Immeasurable Life of the Land of Ultimate Bliss. In the southern Buddha-lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, in each and every land, there are likewise immeasurable, countless bodhisattvas, great beings, and immeasurable, countless hosts of hearers, who with fragrant flowers, banners and streamers, and jeweled canopies come to make offering to the Buddha Immeasurable Life of the Land of Ultimate Bliss. In the western worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, in each and every Buddha-land, there are likewise immeasurable, countless bodhisattvas, great beings, and immeasurable, countless hosts of hearers, who with fragrant flowers, banners and streamers, and jeweled canopies come to make offering to the Buddha Immeasurable Life of the Land of Ultimate Bliss. In the northern Buddha-lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, in each and every Buddha-land, there are likewise immeasurable, countless bodhisattvas, great beings, and immeasurable, countless hosts of hearers, who with fragrant flowers, banners and streamers, and jeweled canopies come to make offering to the Buddha Immeasurable Life of the Land of Ultimate Bliss. In the four intermediate directions, above and below, it is likewise. Each bows at the Buddha’s feet and praises the merit and adornment of that Buddha-land. Thereupon the World-Honored One straightway spoke in verse:
In the eastern worlds, sands of the Ganges, in each and every land, beyond all measure.
Bodhisattvas and hearers bring forth the supreme mind, each with fragrant flowers and jeweled canopies and the rest.
They carry them into the adorned Buddha-land, to make offering to the Tathāgata Immeasurable Life.
Having offered, they bow at his feet and praise him: the supreme, most rare, great field of merit.
Thus in the west, the south, and the north, in the four intermediate directions, above and below, throughout Ganges-sands realms.
The hearers and bodhisattvas are likewise without number, and all with fragrant flowers present their offerings.
Bowing at his feet and circling in reverence, they bear a heart of love and respect, and again praise the depth of the Tathāgata’s past vows.
Accumulating merit, they adorn all things, in the immeasurable, boundless land of Ultimate Bliss.
Though the realms of all Buddhas are majestically adorned, they are hard put to compare with the Tathāgata’s jeweled land.
And again with celestial flowers they make offering to the Buddha; the flowers scatter in the sky and become a canopy,
Its length and breadth a hundred yojanas, its form and marks majestic beyond all compare.
It covers the whole jeweled land of the Tathāgata, and all rejoice together and give rise to delight.
Through a hundred thousand kalpas in the past, they have gathered immeasurable roots of goodness.
They abandon those bodies of the three realms of rebirth, and are brought to the pure land of liberation.
Then that Buddha Immeasurable Life transforms and guides the minds of bodhisattvas from other directions.
Secretly wielding spiritual penetration, he transforms a great radiance; that light streams forth from his face.
Thirty-six koṭis of nayutas of Buddha-lands it shines upon, thousands of koṭis in all.
Having thus shone upon devas and humans everywhere, it re-enters the Tathāgata’s crown of piled hair.
Then all the beings in that assembly reverently sighed at the Buddha’s light, never seen before.
Each and every one brought forth the bodhi mind, vowing to leave the toil of dust and ascend the farther shore.

When the World-Honored One had spoken these verses, among the assembly Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and spoke thus: “World-Honored One, by what cause and condition does the Buddha Immeasurable Life send forth from his face an immeasurable light that illumines all Buddha-lands? May the World-Honored One in skillful means explain it, so that all beings, and the bodhisattvas of other directions, hearing these words, may bring forth a rare and precious mind, turn their will joyfully toward the Buddha’s bodhi, and enter the stage of non-retrogression.”

Thereupon the World-Honored One told Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara: “Listen well now; I shall speak of it for you. That Buddha Tathāgata, immeasurable and boundless asaṃkhyeya kalpas ago, when he was a bodhisattva, made a great vow: When in the future I accomplish true enlightenment, if there are immeasurable beings in worlds of the ten directions who hear my name and title, and whether they bow and recollect me, or praise and take refuge, or make offering of fragrant flowers and the like, such beings shall swiftly be born in my land, and seeing this light shall at once gain liberation. If bodhisattvas see this light, they shall at once receive the prediction and realize the stage of non-retrogression. Holding fragrant flowers and all kinds of offering implements in their hands, they shall go to the boundless pure lands of the ten directions, make offering to the Buddhas and perform the Buddha’s work, increasing their merit. In a moment they shall return to their own land and receive every happiness. Therefore this light enters the Buddha’s crown.”

Again, Ānanda, the tree of bodhi of the Buddha Immeasurable Life, the Worthy and Truly and Fully Enlightened, is one thousand six hundred yojanas high; its branches and leaves spread eight hundred yojanas, and its roots enter the earth five hundred yojanas. Its flowers and fruits open in splendor in immeasurable hundreds of thousands of the colors of precious treasures. Upon that tree are further set the moon-ray maṇi jewel, the Śakra maṇi jewel, the wish-fulfilling maṇi jewel, the sea-holding maṇi jewel, the great green treasure, the sāsatīka treasure, lovable jewelled garlands, great green jewelled garlands, red pearl garlands, blue pearl garlands, and nets of gold and silver treasure — adorned in every kind of way.

Again, Ānanda, at every morning hour a fragrant breeze arises of itself and blows upon this jeweled tree. As the tree is touched and brushed, it gives forth subtle and wondrous sounds. That sound is heard throughout immeasurable worlds, and beings who hear it have no disease of the ear, and even accomplish utmost, perfect bodhi. If there are beings who see this tree, even until they become Buddhas, in the interval between they shall give rise to no disease of the eye. If there are beings who smell the fragrance of the tree, even until they become Buddhas, in the interval between they shall give rise to no disease of the nose. If there are beings who eat the fruit of the tree, even until they become Buddhas, in the interval between their tongue too shall have no disease. If there are beings who are shone upon by the tree’s light, even until they become Buddhas, in the interval between their body too shall have no disease. If there are beings who contemplate and visualize the tree, even until they become Buddhas, in the interval between their mind shall be pure, far from the diseases of affliction such as greed. The Buddha told Ānanda: In such a Buddha-land, the flowers, fruits, trees, and groves all perform the Buddha’s work for beings; all this is embraced by the great past vows of that Buddha.

Again, Ānanda, in that Buddha-land, all the bodhisattvas, great beings, now present and those born in the future, are one life from attaining utmost, perfect bodhi. If there are bodhisattvas who, by their past vows, enter the realm of birth and death to give the lion’s roar and benefit beings, I shall cause them to perform the Buddha’s work as they wish.

Again, Ānanda, in that Buddha-land all the bodhisattvas and all the hearers are fair and dignified in bodily marks, and the circles of their light blaze brightly, shining all around for hundreds of thousands of yojanas. There are two bodhisattvas whose bodily light shines far, illumining the three thousand great thousand worlds.”
Ānanda said: “These two bodhisattvas have great bodily light; what are their names?”

The Buddha told Ānanda: “Of the two bodhisattvas, the first is named Avalokiteśvara, the second is named Great Diligence. They now dwell in this world, bringing great benefit and joy. After the end of their lives, they shall be born in that land.

Again, Ānanda, in that Buddha-land all the bodhisattvas are soft and gentle in countenance, fully endowed with the marks of excellence. In meditative concentration and wisdom they penetrate without obstruction. In spiritual penetration, majesty, and virtue nothing is incomplete. Deeply entering the Dharma gates, they attain the patient acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas. The secret treasuries of the Buddhas they comprehend thoroughly. Taming their faculties, their bodies and minds are soft. Abiding in stillness, they reach the great-vehicle nirvana. Deeply entering right wisdom, they are free of all residual habit. Following the course walked by the Buddhas, they walk the seven factors of the noble path. Cultivating the five eyes, they illumine the real and penetrate the conventional. In eloquence and total retention they are at ease without obstruction. They well understand the boundless skillful means of the world. Their words are true and sincere, deeply entering the flavor of the meaning. Delivering all beings, they expound the right Dharma. Toward the three realms they are equal, free of all discrimination. Without mark, without action, without cause, without fruit. Without grasping, without relinquishing, without bondage, without release. Far from inversion, firm and unmoved as Mount Sumeru. Their wisdom is clear as the brightness of sun and moon. Vast as the sea, bringing forth the treasures of merit. Blazing as fire, burning the fuel of affliction. Patient as the earth, equal toward all things. Pure as water, washing away every dust and defilement. Boundless as space, because they obstruct nothing. Like a lotus rising from the water, because they are free of every stain. Like the crash of thunder, because they give forth the sound of Dharma. Like gathering clouds, because they send down the rain of Dharma. Like wind stirring trees, because they bring forth the sprouts of bodhi. Like the voice of the bull king, because they are unlike other bulls. Like the majesty of dragon and elephant, because they are hard to fathom. Like the gait of a fine horse, because they bear one without mishap. Like the lion’s seat, because they are free of fear. Like the nyagrodha tree, because their shade is great. Like Mount Sumeru, because the eight winds cannot move them. Like the vajra club, because they shatter the mountain of wrong views. Like the body of Brahmā, because they give birth to the hosts of Brahmā. Like the golden-winged bird, because they devour the poisonous dragons. Like birds in the sky, because they have no place of dwelling. Like the contemplation of Maitreya, because they equal the Dharma realm. Such bodhisattvas fill that Buddha-land. They blow the Dharma conch, raise the Dharma banner, beat the Dharma drum, and light the Dharma lamp. Free of fault and pure, without confusion or error, from their hands are born flower garlands and jewelled strings, perfumed ointments and powdered incense, and every kind of offering implement. These they carry to a hundred thousand koṭis of nayutas of Buddha-lands to make offering to the Buddhas. And again from their hands come forth precious flowers in particular, which they scatter in the sky; these transform into jeweled canopies ten yojanas wide, or twenty yojanas, even a hundred thousand yojanas, pervading all Buddha-lands; and in a moment they return to their own land. Without love, without attachment, without grasping, without relinquishing, their bodies and minds are still.

The Buddha told Ānanda: These bodhisattvas are not to be found in my land of the five turbidities. For a hundred thousand koṭis of kalpas it could not be told to the end. The Buddha told Ānanda: In my present land, all the bodhisattvas, great beings, have already made offering to immeasurable Buddhas and planted the roots of every virtue. After the end of their lives, they shall all be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss. Ānanda, rise and join your palms, and bow in homage facing west.”

Thereupon Ānanda rose from his seat, joined his palms, and faced west. In the very act of bowing, he suddenly saw the Land of Ultimate Bliss and the Buddha Immeasurable Life, his countenance vast and broad, his form and marks dignified, like a mountain of gold. And he heard the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, of the worlds of the ten directions praising and extolling the various merits of the Buddha Immeasurable Life.
Ānanda said: “In that pure Buddha-land there is what has never been before; I too would wish and delight to be born in that land.”

The World-Honored One told him: “Those born there are bodhisattvas, great beings, who have already drawn near to immeasurable Buddhas and planted the roots of every virtue. If you wish to be born there, you should with one mind take refuge and gaze in reverence. As he spoke these words, the Buddha Immeasurable Life sent forth from the palm of his hand an immeasurable light that illumined eastward a hundred thousand koṭis of nayutas of Buddha-lands. In this world, all the Black Mountains, Snow Mountains, Golden Mountains, Jewel Mountains, Mount Mucilinda, Great Mount Mucilinda, Mount Sumeru, the Iron Ring Mountain, the Great Iron Ring Mountain, the great seas and rivers, the thickets and groves and trees, and the palaces of devas and humans — every one of these realms was illumined and seen. It was as when the sun rises and lights up the world; so it was likewise.

Thereupon in that assembly, monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans and non-humans, and the rest, all saw the Land of Ultimate Bliss with its various adornments, and saw the Tathāgata Immeasurable Life, surrounded by hearers and bodhisattvas who revered him, like the king of Mount Sumeru rising from the great ocean. Thereupon the Land of Ultimate Bliss, beyond a hundred thousand koṭis of nayutas of lands to the west, by the Buddha’s majestic power appeared as though before their eyes. And they saw that land pure and level, like the surface of the sea, with no hills or ridges or mountain steeps, no grasses or trees or mixed filth. It was adorned only with all kinds of precious treasures, and sages and holy ones dwelt there together.

Again, Ānanda, that Buddha Immeasurable Life, together with the hosts of bodhisattvas and hearers, also all beheld my body and the Sahā world, with its bodhisattvas, hearers, and hosts of humans and devas.”

Thereupon the World-Honored One told Bodhisattva Maitreya: “Do you see the Land of Ultimate Bliss, its merit and adornment, its palaces and pavilions, its gardens and groves and terraces and belvederes, its flowing springs and bathing pools? Maitreya, do you see the devas of the desire realm, up to the Heaven of Ultimate Form, raining all kinds of fragrant flowers that fill the Buddha-land and adorn it? Do you see the bodhisattvas and the hosts of hearers of pure conduct performing the Buddha’s voice and expounding the wondrous Dharma, so that in every Buddha-land the sound is heard and beings gain benefit and joy? Do you see a hundred thousand koṭis of beings roaming in space with their palaces following them?”
